request: Prove one complete Nexus learning loop inside Synthex, first use case the digital business card (Follow the White Rabbit).
head: cb1c5a0f1546cc9350bd1e996ea8a06fcec87dcb (origin/main) on branch feature/learning-loop-white-rabbit

budget.stop_condition: existing components for hypothesis, authority, evidence, experiment and the card are located and both earlier claims are re-verified

gated: push and merge (PC orchestrator; founder brief 18/10/2026 forbids push here)
authority.source: Phill's brief in this session, 18/10/2026: discovery plus reversible local implementation and verification only

altitude.outcome: An attendee who meets Phill leaves with one useful, actionable answer to a real need, and Synthex learns from evidence which front door helps more people, so the next brand decision rests on observed value rather than clicks.

levels.approach: A card page with a DISCOVER door (pick a need, get one action, say if it helped) and a CONNECT door (save contact, approved links), recording outcomes.
levels.value: A working card that helps before it asks for anything.
levels.judge: Playwright journey plus rows in the isolated database.

levels.approach: The same card wired into one complete learning loop on IntentScape: hypothesis, challenge, authorised experiment under a goal contract, observed outcome with uncertainty, deterministic recommendation, and a recorded human decision.
levels.value: The first end-to-end proof that Synthex turns customer evidence into an accountable decision; the pattern every brand can reuse.
levels.judge: Integration test against Postgres: a recorded outcome reaches a recommendation and a decision that only an authorised human can record, with tenant isolation proven.

levels.approach: A cross-brand Nexus learning ledger where each brand's loops feed a shared, consent-bounded decision history.
levels.judge: Needs identity L1 and consent per brand; not yet buildable.

altitude.why: Every piece exists except the loop's outcome-to-decision half; building it on IntentScape events needs no new table, and the card gives it a real, small, inspectable journey. The experimental level is blocked by identity L1, which is scoping only.

depth.practitioner_would: A service designer and an experimentation lead would define the customer outcome first (need identified and an actionable answer received), separate diagnostics from benefit, pre-register the success measure and stop conditions, randomise the comparison, and report intervals rather than point estimates.
depth.raw_material: the Prisma models (IntentScape, LinkBio, experiments, outcome events), the A/B module on main and on the fleet branch, the outcome writer and its callers, the identity L1 scope document, the public-route allowlist
depth.methods: caller trace by git grep, schema read, pre-registration, randomised assignment, Wilson intervals, deterministic decision rules
depth.judge: integration tests on an isolated Postgres plus a browser journey; no model verdict

range.method: three-door journey with the useful action before any contact request
randomised assignment with equivalent offers, pre-registered measure and stop conditions
range.tool: per-session variant recorded on every event

range.method: Wilson score interval per variant and for the difference
append-only events with data class (synthetic, preview, pilot) and revision
no personal data in the slice; random session ids
range.tool: identity L1 scope document as constraint

sources.why: not supplied; kept as unconfirmed configuration

sources.ref: not read by design; isolated local Postgres only

findings.title: Outcome recording still has no production caller
evidence: [VERIFIED command: git grep -l -w recordMarketingAgencyOutcome -- app lib lists only lib/marketing-agency/intelligence/signal-persistence.ts]
findings.consequence: Marketing-agency outcomes are never written in production; the loop's 'observed outcome' step has no existing writer.
findings.action: Do not wire it blindly (it needs a signal id); fleet P6 owns the outcome writer. The card loop records its own outcomes on IntentScape events.

findings.title: The legacy A/B path uses the throwing placeholder on main, not on the fleet branch
evidence: [VERIFIED git show origin/main:lib/ab-testing.ts lines 6 and 78 import createClient from @/lib/platform/noop-client]
[VERIFIED fleet/p3-integrate lib/ab-testing.ts: retired in 63566bad; every persistence path throws ABTestingNotProvisionedError]
[VERIFIED prisma/schema.prisma:4909-4960 SEOExperiment and ExperimentObservation are real persisted tables, so the claim does not generalise]
findings.consequence: The card comparison must not build on lib/ab-testing.ts; it records its own randomised variant.
findings.action: Record variant assignment on each card event; leave A/B storage to a later decision.

findings.title: IntentScape already holds hypothesis, human authority and an append-only evidence log
evidence: [VERIFIED prisma/schema.prisma:2084-2160 IntentScapeHypothesis, IntentScapeGoalContract (immutable human promotion with authorityBoundaries), IntentScapeEvent (append-only, server-written)]
findings.consequence: The learning loop needs no new table; experiment, outcome, recommendation and decision become typed events bound to a goal contract.
findings.action: Build lib/learning-loop on IntentScapeEvent with goal-contract authority checks.

findings.title: LinkBioPage already is a published contact card with approved links
evidence: [VERIFIED prisma/schema.prisma:3183-3250 LinkBioPage and LinkBioLink with isPublished and isVisible]
findings.consequence: CONNECT reuses it; the card adds DISCOVER without duplicating contact data.
findings.action: Read the bio page by slug for profile and visible links; keep its click counters as diagnostics.

findings.title: No digital business card or White Rabbit experience exists
evidence: [VERIFIED command: git grep -l -i -E 'white.?rabbit|business.?card|vcard' -- app lib components matches only dashboard business-overview components]
findings.consequence: The card is new; the smallest slice is DISCOVER plus CONNECT, with SOLVE held as unconfirmed configuration.
findings.action: Build app/card/[slug] with SOLVE disabled until the deck, prize and music are confirmed.

findings.title: A shared identifier is not consent, and identity L1 is not built
evidence: [VERIFIED docs/tier-b/identity-resolution-l1.md: scoping only; cross-brand match is for the pooled frequency cap, NOT for marketing reuse without consent; external client excluded]
findings.consequence: Collecting emails on the card would create a consent and Spam Act obligation the platform cannot yet honour across brands.
findings.action: The slice stores no personal data; email capture waits for a consent design and Phill's approval.

findings.title: A fair story-versus-plain comparison is cheap if assignment is recorded from day one
evidence: [INFERENCE from f2 and f3: a per-session random variant on every event supports a later comparison without A/B tables]
findings.consequence: When the pilot is approved, the first sessions already count toward the comparison.
findings.action: Assign variant per session, keep the substantive offer identical, report Wilson intervals and label data class.

findings.title: Assumption: clicks and shares show the card works
evidence: [VERIFIED app/api/bio/[pageId]/track/route.ts records only view and click counts]
[INFERENCE from the brief's primary measure: benefit is a need identified plus an actionable answer marked useful]
findings.consequence: Click counters stay diagnostics; the loop's primary measure is the useful-answer rate.
findings.action: Keep diagnostics in a separate section of the summary and never feed them to the recommendation.

findings.title: The story card helps at least as many attendees as the plain card
evidence: [UNCONFIRMED no attendee data exists; the pilot is not launched]
findings.consequence: If false, the story adds friction and should be revised or dropped.
findings.action: Pre-register in the experiment record; decide only after the pilot is approved and run.

experiment.precedent: [INFERENCE from the opportunity-map feedback route, which already records a usefulness verdict per public scan]
experiment.prerequisites: pilot approval, at least 60 sessions per variant, equivalent offers
experiment.experiment: randomise story versus plain per session at one event and compare the useful-answer rate with Wilson intervals
experiment.stop_condition: 60 sessions per variant, the event ends, or any consent error or accessibility failure rate above 5 percent
experiment.limit: one event gives a small sample; report the interval and treat the result as directional, not causal proof beyond that audience

top3.rationale: The first complete learning loop, reusable by every brand, no new table.
Gives the loop a real, small customer journey.
Makes the later comparison fair from the first session.

do_nothing.consequence: Synthex keeps hypotheses and goal contracts with no path from outcome to decision, and the card stays an idea.
do_nothing.cost_of_delay: Each event Phill attends without the card is learning not captured; no direct spend.

milestone.promise: One complete learning loop runs locally: an attendee picks a need on the card and gets an action, the outcome is recorded with provenance, a deterministic recommendation is produced, and only an authorised human can record the next decision, all bound to an approved goal contract in one organisation.
scope_out: SOLVE gameplay until the deck, prize and music are confirmed
